summary: Task 03 is implemented exactly as specified: package-level isFilterActive/activeFilterCount with the same predicate as printHeaderCell, a pure clearAllFilters that deletes in place, a thin clearFilters handler that sends on viewCh only when something was removed and calls printCmdline exactly once per path, the corrected setFilter clear branch, the '\' binding on the "sysstat" view and the aligned help line. All three fixed message texts match the user-spec character-for-character and 'Filters: regular expression cleared' is now returned only when a filter was really deleted. go vet and the targeted tests (go test ./top/ -run 'Test_clearFilters|Test_setFilter|Test_activeFilterCount|Test_isFilterActive' -race) are green, gofmt reports no diffs; only two optional follow-ups remain, both about duplication that this task was explicitly forbidden to touch.

suggestions.suggestion: The filter-active predicate now exists twice: as isFilterActive (top/config_view.go:143) and inline in printHeaderCell (top/stat.go:933, 'config.view.Filters[i] != nil && config.view.Filters[i].String() != ""'). They are semantically identical today and the doc comment says they must stay so, but nothing enforces it. stat.go belongs to Task 02 of this wave and was correctly left alone; once that task lands, replace the inline condition in printHeaderCell with isFilterActive(config.view.Filters[i]) so the '*' marker, the cleared-filter counter and the Task 05 cmdline indicator physically cannot drift apart.
suggestions.benefit: Removes the last place where the '*' marker semantics can silently diverge from the counter and the future filter indicator; turns a comment-enforced invariant into a compiler-enforced one.

suggestions.suggestion: clearAllFilters deletes only entries for which isFilterActive is true, so an inactive entry (nil value, or a regexp compiled from an empty pattern) would survive a reported 'Filters: cleared N filter(s)'. That state is unreachable through setFilter today (the empty-answer branch deletes rather than stores, and a non-empty answer can never compile to an empty String()), so this is not a live bug. If you want the post-condition to be unconditional, either delete every key in the loop while counting only the active ones, or state the invariant ('the map never holds inactive entries') in the comment. Worth noting because top/stat.go:1176 isFilterRequired tests only 'v != nil', i.e. it uses a weaker predicate than the one this task standardised.
suggestions.benefit: Makes 'cleared N filter(s)' mean 'the map is now empty' unconditionally, and documents why the weaker isFilterRequired predicate is still safe.
